starters.note: projected = the most likely starter from recent usage and the league's back-to-back rule (hockey/model/ratings.js); actual = the box score's starter

selection.note: total goals is discrete: the central set holding at least 80% probability covers ≥ 80% by construction when calibrated

baseline.what: last season's mean total for every game

slope.what: least squares of the total played on the total projected: 1 = the projections are spread right

variance.what: if calibrated, the variance of the totals played = the variance of the projections + each game's own variance (dispersion 1); above 1 the served distribution is too narrow, below 1 too wide

goalie_status.what: a club's regulation goals ÷ λ, by whether the goalie it faced was the one projected to start (the production price carries no goalie term)

totals.rule: Regular season, out of sample. The projected total is the served distribution's mean (overtime goals and the shootout winner's goal included, as a market total settles); a total of 6.2 means the model expects 6.2 goals, not that 6 or 7 is likely. Real totals vary far more (sd about 2.3) than any forecast can: the useful question is whether the projections' spread matches what is predictable, which the slope (1 = right) and the quintile table answer.

drift.rule: one-sided CUSUM on per-game log loss minus the confirmation mean, allowance half a per-game sd, alarm at 5 sd; WATCH when the season mean sits 2 standard errors above the reference. A monitor: it never retrains or reprices anything.

team_strength.rule: Each club's regulation goals against the regulation λ it was priced at, regular season, out of sample. Slope: Poisson recalibration of goals on log λ (1 = right). TOO_WIDE when the 95% interval sits below 1: the model rates clubs too far apart, overrating the strong and underrating the weak. TOO_NARROW when it sits above 1: too close together. Total and split repeat the slope on the game total and on the home share of goals. Scored ÷ forecast above 1 means the model expected too few goals from that group. A monitor: it never retrains or reprices anything.

standouts.basis: season-to-date numbers from games on earlier dates; ratios to the league's season to date

rows.label: scoring ≥ 1.20× the league (regulation goals a game)
last three games ≥ 1.33× the league's scoring rate
last three games ≤ 0.67× the league's scoring rate
power-play goals a game ≥ 1.35× the league
power-play goals a game ≤ 0.65× the league

summary: selection (17088 team-games): slope 1.01 (95% 0.931–1.09), OK; the highest-λ tenth scored 1.008× its forecast, the lowest 1.011×.
confirmation (14856 team-games): slope 0.889 (95% 0.823–0.956), TOO_WIDE; the highest-λ tenth scored 0.955× its forecast, the lowest 1.018×.
live (374 team-games): slope 1.461 (95% 0.816–2.106), OK; the highest-λ fifth scored 1.073× its forecast, the lowest 0.973×.

clubs.rule: For each club, regulation goals scored (and conceded) against the regulation λ it was priced at, out of sample: this season, last season, the season before and its last 82 games. z = (goals − forecast) ÷ √forecast. A club needs 41 games before it can be flagged; WATCH past |z| 2, FLAG past the two-sided Bonferroni bound over every club and both sides (|z| 3.36 for 64 tests at 5%). PERSISTENT when two windows that share no game (last season and the season before, or last season and this season) both sit past the watch bound on the same side, each with half a season. Goal counts carry score effects and empty nets, so the Poisson z is a guide, not an exact test. A monitor: it flags a possible model issue and never adjusts a rating.
